title: The adjunction $j_!\dashv Lj^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
For a commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$ and an open immersion $j\colon U\to X$ of the setting,
the adjunction

$$
j_!\dashv Lj^*\qquad\text{between }D_{\mathrm{cons}}(U,\Lambda)\text{ and }D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)
$$

of the restricted functors of [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] is the
restriction along the fully faithful inclusions of the ambient adjunction
$D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$, transported along the identification $D(j^*)\cong Lj^*$.

proof.text: Work with module objects over the same pulled-back commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$. The extension-by-zero clause of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] gives the exact functor $j_!=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}$ and the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$. Here the module pullback is the composite $j^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$ specified in [def-sfb-module-upper-star]. The following three steps verify exactness of these two factors for arbitrary $\Lambda$.

source.place: Setting; the underived adjunction needed in the first sentence of the item proof

proof.text: For $T=U,X$, apply [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck] with coefficient category $\Ab$ to obtain that $\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is abelian and has all small colimits. In particular it has equalizers and coequalizers. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] its tensor is closed symmetric monoidal and each fixed-factor tensor functor preserves colimits and is right exact. It is also additive: preservation of zero and binary coproducts preserves the biproduct diagram, and the expression $a+b=\nabla\circ(a\oplus b)\circ\Delta$ for addition then shows preservation of sums. Consequently tensoring by $\Lambda_X$, $j^*\Lambda_X$, or $\Lambda_U$ satisfies all the additive and right-exact tensor hypotheses used below.

source.place: Setting: abelian sheaves, additive and right-exact tensor

proof.text: The abelian-sheaf inverse image $F=j^*_{\Ab}$ is additive and exact by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact], with coefficient category $\mathcal A=\Ab$. The functor $G=\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$ of [def-sfb-modobj-transport] satisfies $U_{j^*\Lambda_X}\circ G=F\circ U_{\Lambda_X}$. Apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] with $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal D=\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal R=\Lambda_X$, and $\mathcal S=j^*\Lambda_X$. Step 2 supplies the abelian and tensor hypotheses. The cited lemma therefore gives additivity and exactness of the transport factor $G$; no separate proof of preservation of kernels or cokernels is being used here.

source.place: Transport: exactness is precisely the existing lifted-exactness lemma

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], $\alpha_j:j^*\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$ is invertible for every condensed ring; [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] identifies it as an isomorphism of ring objects. Thus its source is commutative, since its target $\Lambda_U$ is. In $\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, step 2 supplies the braided closed abelian structure, equalizers, coequalizers, and colimit-preserving additive tensor. Parts 4 and 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], applied to $\alpha_j$ and its inverse, now give $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j^{-1}}$ and exactness of the latter restriction. Hence the extension factor is exact: conjugating an exact image sequence by this natural isomorphism leaves its kernels and cokernels unchanged up to isomorphism. This uses the cited scalar-change theorem, not an assertion that arbitrary scalar extension is exact.

source.place: Extension of scalars: existing scalar-change clauses 4 and 5

proof.text: The composite defining $j^*$ in [def-sfb-module-upper-star] is additive. By steps 3 and 4 both its factors preserve finite limits and finite colimits, so their composite does too. Therefore this specified $j^*$ is exact, for the same arbitrary commutative condensed ring as in step 1.

source.place: Conclusion: compose the two exact factors

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], the two exact functors of steps 1 and 5 send quasi-isomorphisms of complexes to quasi-isomorphisms and give termwise functors $D(j_!)$ and $D(j^*)$ on the unbounded derived categories. The ambient derived pullback $Lj^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] is by definition the total left derived functor, in the left-derived clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], of this same composite $j^*$; since $j^*$ is exact, the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies $Lj^*$ with $D(j^*)$. The derived functors $R(j^*)$ and $L(j_!)$ of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] are defined there by essential constancy; we check directly, without any resolution, that they are everywhere defined with values $D(j^*)K$ and $D(j_!)M$. The system for a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I$ has comparison $D(j^*)(s)^{-1}:D(j^*)I\to D(j^*)K$; for $t:P\to M$, the other system has comparison $D(j_!)(t)^{-1}:D(j_!)M\to D(j_!)P$. These maps are natural, are identities at $s=1_K$ or $t=1_M$, and are all isomorphisms. In [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram] take the distinguished index to be $1_K$, its section to be the identity, and the common index for $s:K\to I$ to be $s$ itself. The arrows of indices are $1_K\to s$, represented by $s$, and $1_s$; the required factorization is $1_{D(j^*)I}=D(j^*)(s)\circ D(j^*)(s)^{-1}$. In [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] take the distinguished index to be $1_M$, its retraction to be the identity, and the common index for $t:P\to M$ to be $t$ itself. The arrows of indices are $t\to1_M$, represented by $t$, and $1_t$; the required factorization is $1_{D(j_!)P}=D(j_!)(t)^{-1}\circ D(j_!)(t)$. Since the comparison at the distinguished index is the identity, the induced map on a morphism $f$ of complexes is $D(j^*)(f)$, resp. $D(j_!)(f)$, and a quasi-isomorphism goes to the inverse of its image. Thus in the sense of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], $R(j^*)=D(j^*)$ and $L(j_!)=D(j_!)$ are everywhere defined.

source.place: first sentence: derive exact functors levelwise

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] (Stacks Tag 09T5) to $G=j_!$ and $F=j^*$, using the underived adjunction of step 1 and the everywhere-defined derived functors of step 6. This gives $L(j_!)\dashv R(j^*)$, and by step 6 these functors are $D(j_!)$ and $D(j^*)$ themselves. Hence the ambient adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ is the one induced by the specified underived adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$, rather than a new choice of an unrelated right adjoint.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; exact-functor identifications as in blueprint proof first sentence

proof.text: Let $\theta:D(j^*)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj^*$ be the inverse of the identification of step 6 of the ambient derived pullback $Lj^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] with $D(j^*)$, given by the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. If $\Phi_{K,L}:\operatorname{Hom}(D(j_!)K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(K,D(j^*)L)$ denotes step 7's ambient Hom-bijection, define $\widetilde\Phi_{K,L}(a)=\theta_L\circ\Phi_{K,L}(a)$. Its inverse sends $b:K\to Lj^*L$ to $\Phi_{K,L}^{-1}(\theta_L^{-1}\circ b)$. The two inverse identities follow by cancellation of $\theta_L$ and $\theta_L^{-1}$, and naturality is explicit: for $u:K\to K_1$, $v:L\to L_1$ and $a:D(j_!)K_1\to L$, one has $\widetilde\Phi_{K,L_1}(v\circ a\circ D(j_!)(u))=\theta_{L_1}\circ D(j^*)(v)\circ\Phi_{K_1,L}(a)\circ u=Lj^*(v)\circ\widetilde\Phi_{K_1,L}(a)\circ u$. This explicitly constructs $D(j_!)\dashv Lj^*$.

source.place: second sentence: transport the right adjoint

proof.text:
Write $\iota_U$ and $\iota_X$ for the inclusions of the bounded constructible categories. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] these are full subcategories, with the same Hom-sets as the ambient derived categories. The definitions [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] give the restricted functors and their comparison with the ambient functors after inclusion for the general coefficient ring $\Lambda$. In particular, the current extension-by-zero definition equips each object $D(j_!)(\iota_U K)$ with its bounded-constructibility property and gives the inclusion comparison with identity components. We use its inverse as the comparison $c$ below, so the direction agrees with the Hom formulas. For $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(U,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$, define the required Hom-bijection by the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)}(j_!K,L)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})}(D(j_!)\iota_UK,\iota_XL)
\xrightarrow{\ \widetilde\Phi\ }
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})}(\iota_UK,Lj^*\iota_XL)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{cons}}(U,\Lambda)}(K,Lj^*L).$$
Here the equalities use the inclusion comparisons, or equivalently the corresponding canonical Hom-bijections if restrictions commute up to isomorphism. More explicitly, put $F=D(j_!)$, $G=Lj^*$, $f=j_!$ and $g=Lj^*$ for the last two restricted functors. Write the natural inclusion comparisons as $c_K:F\iota_UK\xrightarrow{\sim}\iota_X(fK)$ and $d_L:G\iota_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}\iota_U(gL)$. The displayed map sends $a:fK\to L$ to the unique $b:K\to gL$ with $\iota_U(b)=d_L\circ\widetilde\Phi(\iota_X(a)\circ c_K)$. Its inverse sends $b$ to the unique $a$ with $\iota_X(a)=\widetilde\Phi^{-1}(d_L^{-1}\circ\iota_U(b))\circ c_K^{-1}$. Full faithfulness gives these unique morphisms, and cancellation of $c,c^{-1},d,d^{-1}$ and the two ambient inverse identities proves the two restricted inverse identities. For $u:K'\to K$ and $v:L\to L'$, write $\Psi$ for this restricted map. Naturality of $c$, step 8, and naturality of $d$ give, in order,
$$\iota_U\Psi(v\circ a\circ f(u))=d_{L'}\circ G(\iota_Xv)\circ\widetilde\Phi(\iota_Xa\circ c_K)\circ\iota_Uu=\iota_U(g(v))\circ d_L\circ\widetilde\Phi(\iota_Xa\circ c_K)\circ\iota_Uu=\iota_U(g(v)\circ\Psi(a)\circ u).$$
Faithfulness of $\iota_U$ proves naturality in both variables. This defines the adjunction in the statement. For the ambient unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ of step 8, the restricted unit and counit are characterized by $\iota_U(\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K)=d_{fK}\circ G(c_K)\circ\eta_{\iota_UK}$ and $\iota_X(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L)=\varepsilon_{\iota_XL}\circ F(d_L^{-1})\circ c_{gL}^{-1}$. Thus these are precisely the ambient unit and counit restricted using the inclusion comparisons. For the left triangle, naturality of $c$ gives $\iota_X(f(\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K))=c_{gfK}\circ F(\iota_U\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K)\circ c_K^{-1}$. Substitute the unit and counit formulas and cancel $c_{gfK}^{-1}c_{gfK}$ and $d_{fK}^{-1}d_{fK}$; naturality of $\varepsilon$ then gives
$$\iota_X(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_{fK}\circ f(\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K))=\varepsilon_{\iota_XfK}\circ FG(c_K)\circ F(\eta_{\iota_UK})\circ c_K^{-1}=c_K\circ\varepsilon_{F\iota_UK}\circ F(\eta_{\iota_UK})\circ c_K^{-1}=1.$$
For the right triangle, naturality of $d$ gives $\iota_U(g(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L))=d_L\circ G(\iota_X\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L)\circ d_{fgL}^{-1}$. Substitution cancels $d_{fgL}^{-1}d_{fgL}$ and $G(c_{gL}^{-1}c_{gL})$, and naturality of $\eta$ gives
$$\iota_U(g(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L)\circ\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_{gL})=d_L\circ G(\varepsilon_{\iota_XL})\circ GF(d_L^{-1})\circ\eta_{\iota_UgL}=d_L\circ G(\varepsilon_{\iota_XL})\circ\eta_{G\iota_XL}\circ d_L^{-1}=1.$$
The last equality in each calculation is the corresponding ambient triangle identity. Faithfulness of the inclusions proves both restricted triangle identities.
